# nRF54LM20-DK firmware v0.8.0

Four-path capability in every shipped image, and the `a1_1` → `a1_4` rename.

## Highlights

- **Every image is now four-path-capable.** All eight nRF54LM20-DK presets
  build with `boards/4_path_1_local.conf`:
  `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_SDC_CS_MAX_ANTENNA_PATHS=4` with
  `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_SDC_CS_NUM_ANTENNAS=1`. The DK still has one antenna; the
  four-path maximum is the controller's capability, not a claim of four
  physical antennas. The negotiated tone configuration follows the **peer's**
  antenna count — from the initiator's side `A1_B1` against a one-antenna peer
  up to `A1_B4` against a four-antenna peer; the reflector sees the same link
  as `An_B1`.
- **Renamed from `a1_1` to `a1_4`.** Every preset, build directory and
  release image moves from `<board>[_usb]_<cent|peri>_a1_1` to
  `<board>[_usb]_<cent|peri>_a1_4`. Update any script that pins an archive
  file name from an earlier release; the eight role/mode/transport
  combinations are otherwise unchanged.
- **No transport or wire-format change.** The COBS stream, buffer sizes
  (29,000 B run, 32 KiB USB data FIFO, 4,800 B CS reassembly) and both
  transports are unchanged.

## Mixed-pair interop evidence

The four-path capability was proven on the bench before it became the shipped
policy. The mixed LM20↔nRF54L15 campaign built the capability into the
interop images in [#35](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/issues/35),
re-baselined the LM20↔LM20 pair at `A1_B1` in
[#37](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/issues/37), smoked the
mixed pair at `A1_B2` in
[#38](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/issues/38), and gated it
for 600 s in
[#39](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/issues/39). Across those
runs the per-procedure payload stayed at 26,666 bytes against 26,669 for the
one-path `A1_B1` pair — a value-variance difference, not a payload growth —
which is why the transport sizing did not change with the capability.

The released images were then re-gated on the LM20↔LM20 pair in
[#41](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/issues/41). The full gate
tables and the A1_B2 console excerpts are recorded on those issues and in
[docs/bench-tag-interop.md](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/blob/v0.8.0/docs/bench-tag-interop.md#a1_b2-600-s-gate-evidence-39).

## Supported hardware

- **nRF54LM20-DK** (PCA10184), target `nrf54lm20dk/nrf54lm20a/cpuapp`.
- Built as the **A** variant (`nRF54LM20A`), the NPU-less variant for the
  B-silicon DK (`SOC_NRF54LM20A_DEVELOP_IN_NRF54LM20B`). The firmware does not
  use the NPU, so the A target runs on both silicon flavors.
- One 2.4 GHz trace antenna and one RF path; no antenna switch and no RF
  supply rail. Four antenna paths are supported by the controller.
- The bench boards are engineering-sample A silicon (`nRF54LM20A ENGA`).

| Transport | COBS data | Console |
|-----------|-----------|---------|
| Native USB (recommended) | Initiator CDC ACM function `if00` (label `CS Data`) | Initiator `if02`; reflector `if00` (label `Console`) |
| J-Link VCOM (compatibility) | VCOM0 (`uart30`), 1,000,000 baud, 8N1, no flow control | VCOM1 (`uart20`), 115200 baud |

The native USB link negotiates 480 Mbit/s high speed on the DK. A
full-speed-only host falls back to 12 Mbit/s, which works but is parity-only
and does not meet the transport-headroom criterion. CDC ACM ignores the
configured baud rate; open the data port at 1,000,000 baud to match the VCOM
workflow.

## Firmware variants

`cs-ranging-firmware.zip` contains **eight images**: four VCOM and four native
USB. Every image name changed from `a1_1` to `a1_4`.

| File | Role | Mode | Preset | Transport |
|------|------|------|--------|-----------|
| `initiator_nrf54lm20dk_cent_a1_4.hex` | Initiator | RAS | `nrf54lm20dk_cent_a1_4` | J-Link VCOM |
| `reflector_nrf54lm20dk_peri_a1_4.hex` | Reflector | RAS | `nrf54lm20dk_peri_a1_4` | J-Link VCOM |
| `initiator_nrf54lm20dk_cent_a1_4_ipt.hex` | Initiator | IPT | `nrf54lm20dk_cent_a1_4_ipt` | J-Link VCOM |
| `reflector_nrf54lm20dk_peri_a1_4_ipt.hex` | Reflector | IPT | `nrf54lm20dk_peri_a1_4_ipt` | J-Link VCOM |
| `initiator_nrf54lm20dk_usb_cent_a1_4.hex` | Initiator | RAS | `nrf54lm20dk_usb_cent_a1_4` | Native USB |
| `reflector_nrf54lm20dk_usb_peri_a1_4.hex` | Reflector | RAS | `nrf54lm20dk_usb_peri_a1_4` | Native USB |
| `initiator_nrf54lm20dk_usb_cent_a1_4_ipt.hex` | Initiator | IPT | `nrf54lm20dk_usb_cent_a1_4_ipt` | Native USB |
| `reflector_nrf54lm20dk_usb_peri_a1_4_ipt.hex` | Reflector | IPT | `nrf54lm20dk_usb_peri_a1_4_ipt` | Native USB |

Flash a **matched** pair: the same ranging mode (RAS **or** IPT) and the same
transport. The two modes use different BLE discovery and do not pair with
each other.

## Install

The full procedure is in the
[flash quickstart](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/blob/v0.8.0/docs/flash-quickstart.md).
In short:

1. Download `cs-ranging-firmware.zip` from this release and unpack it.
2. Flash one DK with the initiator image and one with the reflector image
   through the on-board J-Link (`nrfutil device program --firmware <file>.hex`
   or the nRF Connect Programmer app).
3. For native USB, disconnect the J-Link cable and run each DK from its native
   USB port. On Linux,
   `/dev/serial/by-id/usb-Metirionic_Mars_CS_Initiator_<serial>-if00` is the
   data port and `...-if02` the console;
   `/dev/serial/by-id/usb-Metirionic_Mars_CS_Reflector_<serial>-if00` is the
   reflector console. Open the data port at 1,000,000 baud, 8N1.
4. For J-Link VCOM, keep the J-Link cable connected: VCOM0 at 1,000,000 baud
   carries the COBS stream, VCOM1 at 115200 the console.

## Validation

### Archive

`cs-ranging-firmware.zip` (2,699,717 bytes, sha256 `da650da8…`) was downloaded
from this release and verified to contain exactly the eight images above —
four VCOM and four native USB, all under the new `a1_4` names.

### Released-image bench gate (#41)

The v0.8.0 **native-USB** archive images were re-gated on the physical
LM20↔LM20 bench pair on 2026-10-27. Both default-cadence runs used the exact
release `.hex` files and started from a fresh boot; the interval-1 headroom
run uses a manual bench build of the v0.8.0 tree, because release builds keep
the default procedure interval. The four VCOM images are the same firmware on
the compatibility transport and are unchanged by the four-path policy; this
re-gate exercises the native-USB images, and the archive check above covers
all eight.

| Run | Images | Serialization runs | Valid frames | Event frames | Invalid | Empty proc. | Reflector aborts | Watchdog (init/refl) | Backlog (serialize/diag) | USB drops | Wire rate | Result |
|-----|--------|-------------------:|-------------:|-------------:|--------:|------------:|-----------------:|----------------------|--------------------------|----------:|-----------|--------|
| USB RAS, 600 s | released USB RAS pair | 1847 | 5546 | 3697 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 | 0.657 Mbit/s | PASS |
| USB IPT, 600 s | released USB IPT pair | 1835 | 5510 | 3673 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 | 0.653 Mbit/s | PASS |
| USB RAS interval 1, 600 s | released USB RAS reflector + bench initiator | 9119 | 27410 | 18239 | 0 | 21\* | 0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 | 3.242 Mbit/s | Reference met\*\* |

Both default-cadence runs negotiated `A1_B1` (`peer antennas: 1`, antenna
configuration index 0) at the default procedure interval 10, and every
transport assertion passed: 480 Mbit/s link, zero USB transport drops, zero
serialize and diagnostic backlog, zero reflector aborts, zero watchdog
recoveries, and zero invalid COBS frames. In the RAS measured capture the
best-effort USB console ring dropped the negotiation block, so that block is
recorded by an immediate-attach console-only smoke on the same release image;
the IPT measured capture shows it directly.

\* The 21 empty-procedure signatures are the CS scheduler at the clamped
interval-2 cadence — the same signal the original reference recorded (21);
the harness's generic assertion reports `FAIL` at interval 1 by design. The
transport criteria (wire rate and drop count) pass.

\*\* The interval-1 run applied the controller's clamped `procedure interval:
2` and measured **405,283.6 B/s = 3.242 Mbit/s**, 0.25 % below the
3.250 Mbit/s reference from
[#20](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/issues/20), with zero USB
transport drops, zero backlog, zero reflector aborts, and zero watchdog
recoveries. One earlier attempt was invalidated by a foreign CS initiator
that connected to the reflector; a second was rerun from a clean start after
a 58-abort `NO_CS_SYNC_RECEIVED` burst on the reflector coincided with its
console reader hanging up (reflector capture status 0, not 124). The reported
run is the clean re-measurement.

After the gate the pair is left flashed with the released native-USB **RAS**
images, freshly booted at 480 Mbit/s, connected and streaming; the nRF54L15
TAG used for the interop campaign is left halted.

## Known issues and constraints

- **High speed is experimental in NCS v3.4.0.** Nordic describes high-speed
  support that way; the bench measured a working 480 Mbit/s link on the DK.
- **Full speed is parity-only.** The 12 Mbit/s fallback carries the same data
  and console but does not meet the transport-headroom criterion.
- **NCSDK-38624.** CDC ACM serial initialization at boot can hang an
  nRF54LM20 until the USB cable is disconnected. USB builds disable that path
  (`CONFIG_CDC_ACM_SERIAL_INITIALIZE_AT_BOOT=n`) and enable the UDC on VBUS
  attach instead. This is an avoidance, not an SDK fix.
- **DRGN-29129.** USB high speed shares HFCLK24M with MPSL; USB is initialized
  after the BLE stack to keep the MPSL ordering safe.
- **DRGN-29277 is deferred.** The sleep-current workaround after USB
  disconnect is not in this release. HFCLK24M remains active while USB is in
  use, so sleep-current targets need the follow-up power-management work.
- **VBUS removal is designed but bench-tested only indirectly.** The UDC
  disables on the VBUS-removed message without a reboot; the gate exercised
  boot with no host and a host stall/close, not a literal port-power removal.
- **The console is best-effort.** Its 1 KiB TX ring and the bounded deferred
  log queue can delay or drop messages, especially before enumeration. Open
  the data port before or at boot to capture the first procedures.
- **The USB identity uses development IDs.** VID `0x1915` and PIDs `0x0001` /
  `0x0002` are Nordic development values; a USB-IF VID/PID remains pre-product
  work.
- **Windows and macOS coverage is manual.** Linux is the merge and release
  gate; the other hosts are release smoke tests
  ([#24](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/issues/24)).
- **Programming and recovery stay on SWD.** There is no USB bootloader or DFU
  interface and MCUboot is not used; USB host mode is not available.
- **Do not open the VCOM data port at 921600.** The DK's J-Link bridge
  supports up to 1 Mbps and explicitly does not support 921600; the firmware
  uses 1,000,000 baud.
- **Secure application-core only.** TF-M and non-secure-image USB ownership
  are unverified; the supported builds are the `.../cpuapp` targets.

## Compatibility

- The COBS wire format and the `mars-bluetooth-hci` API are unchanged; the
  same host decoder works over both transports and both path capabilities.
- The **release artifact names changed** (`a1_1` → `a1_4`). Scripts that pin a
  file name from an earlier release must update; the in-archive contents are
  otherwise the same eight role/mode/transport combinations.
- The actual antenna-path count in a procedure follows the peer, not the
  preset name. An `a1_4` image paired with a one-antenna peer still runs
  `A1_B1`; it gains paths only against a multi-antenna peer.
- Both transports ship in one archive. Use VCOM for hosts without native USB,
  for a J-Link-only setup, or as the A/B comparison basis.
